I was thinking that there are some general inputs and there are some inputs required per run correct? 

So each run should ask me that first, once we confirm, then it hsould produce the resuts. 

Does it make sense?

messages.text: Yes, that makes sense, and it's the right split. **General inputs** (Inputs tab) are set once. **Each run starts with a brief**: its own questions, and nothing runs until you confirm. Run 3's brief is in the Run 3 tab: B1 audiences, B2 theme (October means midterms for students and holiday/Black Friday prep for small biz), B3 bring back the 6 earlier survivors, B4 anything extra, and **B5 Confirm**. When B5 says Confirmed and you press Send, I start.

comments.text:
Why dont I have the option to select the audience and everything.

Imagine this is our fresh run and it must select ideas that are not in our Selected Ideas.

messages.text: You're right, I shouldn't have assumed. Run 3 is now a **fresh run**. **B1** lists all 13 audiences with **none ticked**, and B2 (theme) is unpicked too. I removed the "bring back old ideas" question. There's a new **Selected Ideas** tab (0 so far): ideas you Keep in a run move there, and runs skip anything already in it.

comments.text:
So maybe you The Run3 Inputs should be here. 

And you can remove the inputs tab what you think?

messages.text: Agreed, done. **The Inputs tab is gone.** Every input now lives in each run's brief (B1–B8). Your earlier answers carried over only where you'd actually given them: build types, 10 ideas, no startup remix, parallel research. Budget (/bin/zsh) is now a note under S1 in the Sources tab. Tabs: Plan · Sources · Run 3 · Selected Ideas.

comments.anchorText: B2: A theme for this run?

messages.text: Done. B2 is now multi-select, and your pick (**Saving them time**) carried over. Tick as many themes as you like. Send stays at "Nothing to send" until you change something.

comments.anchorText: B1: Who is this run for?
comments.text:
I really feel that we can have more options in an option.
So like small business owners of what?
Real estate, restaurant, salons etc etc.

Correct? 
So how can we make B1 descriptive, what do you think?

messages.text: Yes, correct, and done. **B1 now has two levels**: tick an audience, and its specific groups open right under it. Small business shows 12 (restaurants and cafés, salons, real estate, trades, cleaning, local shops, online sellers, gyms, clinics, photographers, coaches, accountants). Students, creators, freelancers and parents have theirs too. Leave the groups blank to mean "all of them". I'd tick **restaurants and cafés, salons, and trades**: huge, poorly served by software, and very visual on camera. Unticking an audience also unticks its groups.
